breakfast.name: Mas Huni (Tuna and Coconut)
instructions: Mix shredded tuna with coconut, onion, chili, lime
Serve with hot roshi
breakfast.description: Maldives' national breakfast — smoked tuna mixed with fresh coconut.

breakfast.name: Roshi (Flatbread)
instructions: Mix dough, rest 10 min
Roll thin circles
Cook on tawa until golden spots
Brush with oil
breakfast.description: Thin flatbread cooked on a tawa.

breakfast.name: Roshi (Flatbread)
instructions: Mix flour, water, salt into a smooth, soft dough
Rest 20 minutes
Divide into balls, roll thin — thinner than Indian roti
Dry fry on a hot tava — small brown spots on both sides
The roshi is thin and slightly charred in spots
Serve with fresh coconut paste (dhiyaa hakuru) or tuna curry
Roshi is the everyday Maldivian bread — found at every meal alongside rice or curries
The Maldivian roshi is thinner than Sri Lankan or Indian roti
It's used to scoop up curry — no cutlery
The Indian Ocean trade route brought flatbread-making to the Maldives
breakfast.description: The Maldives' everyday flatbread — thin flour dough dry-fried until lightly charred, served alongside tuna curry or coconut paste at breakfast. Thinner than Indian roti. Used to scoop curries rather than as an accompaniment. Indian Ocean trade routes (India, Sri Lanka, Arabia) brought flatbread culture to the atolls.

breakfast.name: Dhiyaa Hakuru (Fresh Coconut Paste)
instructions: Grate fresh coconut — the freshness is essential
Mix with lime juice, chili, salt
Optional: add chopped curry leaves, fried shallots
The result is a fresh, moist coconut condiment — not dried, not cooked
The coconut paste is cold and bright, crunchy with shredded coconut
Dhiyaa hakuru is the standard Maldivian breakfast condiment
Served alongside roshi, rice, or any Maldivian breakfast
The lime keeps it bright; the chili adds heat against the sweet coconut
The Maldives has abundant coconut palms on every atoll
This is coconut at its freshest — from tree to table same day
breakfast.description: The Maldives' fresh coconut condiment — freshly grated coconut mixed with lime juice, chili, and salt. Served alongside roshi or rice at breakfast. The freshness is the point: coconut grated the same morning, lime for brightness, chili for heat. The Maldives' abundant coconut palms make this the most available and immediate flavor on the islands.

lunch.name: Garudhiya (Tuna Broth)
instructions: Boil tuna chunks with curry and pandan leaves
Add chili and onion
Simmer 15 min
Serve over rice with lime, chili, and onion
lunch.description: Clear, aromatic tuna broth — the Maldivian daily staple.

lunch.name: Bis Keemiya (Egg Rolls)
ingredients: Filling: hard-boiled eggs, cabbage, onion, chili, curry leaves
instructions: Mix filling
Fill wrappers, roll tightly
Deep fry until golden

lunch.name: Rihaakuru (Concentrated Tuna Paste)
ingredients: Skipjack tuna (fresh, large amount — it reduces dramatically)
instructions: Rihaakuru is the Maldivian equivalent of fish sauce — but as a paste, not a liquid
Boil tuna in salted water until fully cooked
Strain the liquid (which is already the beginning of rihaakuru)
Continue boiling the strained liquid — it reduces for hours
The liquid reduces from a large pot to a very small, very dark, very concentrated paste
The final rihaakuru is dark brown, intensely savory, salty, with deep fishy umami
It stores for months at room temperature — a preserved flavor concentrate
One spoonful flavors an entire dish
Rihaakuru is used as a flavoring, a condiment, and eaten with rice
The smell is very intense — divisive but beloved by Maldivians
This is the Maldives' most distinctive food product
lunch.description: The Maldives' ancient flavor concentrate — skipjack tuna boiled, strained, and the liquid reduced for hours until it becomes a thick, dark paste of extraordinary umami intensity. Rihaakuru stores for months, flavors any dish, and is the Maldives' most distinctive food product. One spoonful transforms plain rice into a complete meal. The smell is intense; the flavor is irreplaceable.

lunch.name: Mas Riha (Tuna Curry)
ingredients: Skipjack tuna (fresh or dried smoked — kiru mas)
instructions: Fry onion, garlic, ginger with curry leaves until fragrant
Add turmeric, cumin, chili — bloom the spices
Add tuna (fresh cubed or dried-smoked kiru mas, rehydrated)
Add coconut milk — it should submerge the fish
Add pandan leaf for fragrance
Simmer 20-25 minutes
Optional: add rihaakuru — it deepens the flavor dramatically
Mas riha is Maldives' national everyday curry
Eaten with roshi or rice at least once daily by most Maldivians
The tuna is the central protein — always tuna, never varying
The curry leaves, coconut milk, and pandan combination is the Maldivian flavor signature
lunch.description: The Maldives' national everyday curry — skipjack tuna in a coconut milk curry with curry leaves, pandan, and turmeric. Eaten at least once daily by most Maldivians, this is the taste of the islands. Optionally deepened with rihaakuru (concentrated tuna paste). The curry leaf-pandan-coconut combination is the Maldivian flavor identity.

dinner.name: Rihaakuru Mash
instructions: Mix rihaakuru with diced onion, chili, lime juice
Spread on hot roshi
Serve with tea

dinner.name: Mas Riha (Tuna Curry)
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, curry leaves
Add spices and coconut milk
Add tuna chunks
Simmer 15 min
Serve with rice

dinner.name: Bis Keemiya (Tuna Pastry)
ingredients: Pastry dough (wheat flour, oil, water — thin)
instructions: Make a thin, pliable pastry dough
Filling: mix flaked tuna with chopped hard-boiled egg, fried onion, chili, curry leaves
Roll dough thin, cut into circles
Fill each circle with tuna mixture
Fold into a half-moon, press edges to seal
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Bis keemiya is the Maldivian stuffed pastry — a snack or light meal
The half-moon shape is the signature form
The curry-leaf-tuna filling is entirely Maldivian
dinner.description: The Maldives' tuna pastry — thin dough filled with flaked tuna, hard-boiled egg, and curry leaves, folded into half-moons and deep-fried. The curry leaf-tuna filling is the Maldivian signature. Bis keemiya are sold at shops and eaten as street food throughout the atolls.

dinner.name: Fihunu Mas (Grilled Tuna)
ingredients: Skipjack tuna (steaks or whole small fish)
instructions: Marinate tuna in garlic, ginger, chili, lime, salt, coconut oil — 30 minutes minimum
Grill over charcoal or under high broiler
Tuna is forgiving for grilling — its high fat content keeps it moist
But don't overcook — it should be just barely cooked through, slightly pink in thick parts
The grill marks and slight char are the point
Squeeze lime over finished fish
The simplest preparation of Maldivian tuna — the fish's quality speaks directly
Skipjack from the Maldivian fishery is some of the freshest tuna in the Indian Ocean
The Maldives has one of the world's most sustainably managed tuna fisheries
Grilled tuna with chili and lime is the Maldivian grill
dinner.description: The Maldives' grilled tuna — skipjack tuna marinated in garlic, ginger, chili, and lime, grilled until charred outside and barely cooked through. The Maldivian tuna fishery is among the world's most sustainable (traditional pole-and-line fishing). Maldivian skipjack at peak freshness, grilled simply, is the cleanest expression of Indian Ocean tuna.

dinner.name: Saagu Bondibai (Sago Pudding)
instructions: Cook sago pearls in water until translucent — they turn from white to clear
Drain, add coconut milk
Add palm sugar or white sugar to taste
Pandan leaf for fragrance — steep then remove
Cardamom adds warmth
Serve warm or cold — both work
Saagu bondibai is the Maldivian dessert-snack — simple, sweet, satisfying
The coconut milk-pandan combination is the Indian Ocean dessert signature
Found across Maldives, Sri Lanka, and Indonesia — the same coconut-sago idea
The pearl-like texture of sago in coconut milk is the textural pleasure
dinner.description: The Maldives' coconut sago pudding — translucent sago pearls in sweetened coconut milk with pandan and cardamom. The coconut milk-pandan combination is the Indian Ocean dessert signature, shared with Sri Lanka and Indonesia. The pearl texture of cooked sago in rich coconut milk is the defining textural pleasure.

snacks.name: Gulha (Fish Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: smoked tuna, coconut, onion, chili, ginger
instructions: Make rice flour dough
Fill with spiced tuna-coconut mixture
Shape into rounds
Deep fry until golden
snacks.description: Crispy rice-flour dumplings with smoked tuna.

snacks.name: Kulhi Boakibaa (Fish Cake)
instructions: Grind soaked rice into a rough paste
Mix with shredded tuna, grated coconut, onion, curry leaves, chili, ginger, cumin, turmeric
Press into an oiled pan — about 2 cm thick
Bake or steam until set
Cut into squares or diamonds
Kulhi boakibaa is the Maldivian fish cake — rice-tuna-coconut bound together
The grated coconut is structural and flavor-adding
The rice paste (not flour) gives a specific texture — moist and dense
A standard item at any Maldivian tea time or gathering
The diamond cut is traditional — they're served at celebrations and daily alike
snacks.description: The Maldives' fish cake — soaked rice ground and mixed with shredded tuna, grated coconut, and curry leaves, pressed and baked or steamed until set, cut in diamonds. The rice paste (not flour) gives a dense, moist texture. Kulhi boakibaa is the standard Maldivian tea-time item: at every gathering, every celebration.

snacks.name: Gulha (Tuna Dumplings)
instructions: Mix filling: flaked tuna, fresh coconut, onion, curry leaves, chili
Wrap in small balls of dough — completely enclosed
Deep fry until golden
Gulha are small, perfectly round tuna-coconut dumplings
The spherical shape is the visual signature — perfectly round
The fresh coconut-tuna combination inside the crispy shell is the key contrast
Gulha are Maldives' most recognizable snack — sold at every shop and teahouse
The round shape and tuna-coconut filling are instantly recognizable as Maldivian
Eaten with hot tea or coffee
snacks.description: The Maldives' round tuna dumpling — flaked tuna and fresh grated coconut wrapped inside dough spheres and deep-fried. The perfectly spherical shape is the visual signature. The tuna-fresh coconut combination inside the crispy shell is the Maldivian snack identity. Sold at every teahouse and shop across the atolls.

snacks.name: Hedhikaa (Short Eats)
ingredients: Various: bis keemiya pastry, gulha, kulhi boakibaa, roshi
instructions: Hedhikaa refers to the collection of short-eat snacks served at Maldivian tea time
Every afternoon, Maldivians gather for tea with a selection of hedhikaa
The individual components (bis keemiya, gulha, kulhi boakibaa) are each described above
The hedhikaa spread is the social institution: friends, family, neighbors over tea and snacks
Teahouses (hotaa) serve hedhikaa throughout the day
The variety of snacks is the point — sampling several together
Hedhikaa are also sold individually at shops
The culture of afternoon tea with short eats connects the Maldives to its Sri Lankan and South Asian neighbors
But the Maldivian versions are always tuna-and-coconut-based — uniquely atoll food
snacks.description: The Maldives' tea-time spread — a selection of tuna-and-coconut short eats (bis keemiya, gulha, kulhi boakibaa) served alongside sweet tea. The afternoon hedhikaa gathering at teahouses is the Maldivian social institution. The shared culture of 'short eats with tea' connects the Maldives to its Sri Lankan neighbors — but every component is filled with tuna and coconut.

desserts.name: Bondi (Sweet Coconut Balls)
instructions: Cook coconut with sugar, stirring constantly
Add cardamom and rose water
When thick, shape into balls
Let cool
desserts.description: Caramelized coconut balls flavored with cardamom.

desserts.name: Foni Boakibaa (Sweet Rice Cake)
instructions: Mix rice flour with coconut milk, sugar, pandan extract, cardamom
The pandan gives natural green color — grind pandan leaves in water, strain for the extract
Pour into an oiled pan
Steam or bake — steam gives a more tender result
The rice cake should be green from the pandan and fragrant from cardamom
Cut into squares or diamonds
Foni boakibaa is the sweet companion to kulhi boakibaa (the fish cake)
The same rice cake base, sweet instead of savory — the Maldivian cake dichotomy
Pandan is the fragrance of Maldivian sweet cooking
Served at celebrations, alongside tea, and as dessert
desserts.description: The Maldives' pandan rice cake — rice flour mixed with coconut milk, pandan extract (natural green coloring and fragrance), and cardamom, steamed until set. The sweet companion to kulhi boakibaa (the savory fish cake) — same technique, opposite flavor. Pandan is the Maldivian sweet kitchen's defining fragrance.

desserts.name: Dhonkeyo Kajuru (Banana Fritters)
instructions: Mash ripe bananas
Mix with flour, sugar, coconut milk into a thick batter
Fry spoonfuls until golden
Dhonkeyo kajuru is the Maldivian banana fritter
Same concept as throughout the Indian Ocean region (Indonesia, Malaysia, East Africa)
The coconut milk in the batter is the Maldivian touch
The deep banana sweetness against the slightly crispy exterior is the pleasure
Eaten as a snack or after dinner
The Maldives grows a specific small, intensely sweet banana variety on many atolls
desserts.description: The Maldives' banana fritter — overripe banana in a coconut milk batter, fried until golden. The coconut milk batter is the Maldivian touch. The small, intensely sweet Maldivian banana variety makes the best fritters. Eaten as a snack or a dessert after curry.

drinks.name: Raa (Palm Toddy)
instructions: Collect sap from coconut palm at dawn
Serve fresh and sweet
Or let ferment for mild alcohol
drinks.description: Fresh coconut palm sap — sweet or fermented.

drinks.name: Sai (Maldivian Tea)
instructions: Brew strong black tea
Add condensed milk and sugar
Serve in short glasses

drinks.name: Kanaa Bai (Toddy Palm Fresh Sap)
ingredients: Fresh toddy palm sap (tapped from palm flower stems — kanaa)
instructions: Toddy (kanaa) is tapped from palm trees on the atolls — collected fresh at dawn
Fresh toddy is mildly sweet, cloudy, naturally carbonated (slightly effervescent)
Drink immediately — it ferments quickly
The natural faint fizz and sweetness is the fresh-toddy experience
After 12-24 hours it becomes alcoholic palm wine
The Maldives is officially a dry country (alcohol prohibited for citizens)
But fresh toddy (kanaa) is not prohibited — it's essentially a juice when fresh
Fresh kanaa has been the Maldivian islands' natural drink for centuries
The sweet, slightly fizzy palm sap on a hot atoll day is both refreshing and nutritious
drinks.description: The Maldives' ancient palm drink — fresh sap from the cut flower stems of coconut palms, drunk immediately before fermentation. Naturally slightly fizzy and mildly sweet. The Maldives is officially alcohol-free for citizens, but fresh kanaa (not yet fermented) is legal and traditional. Tapped at dawn, drunk the same morning — one of the Indian Ocean's oldest beverages.
